PSAL. CXIX. 71.
It is good for me that I have been afflicted; that I might learn thy Statutes.

THE Context speaketh of Afflictions by occasion of Persecutions; The Proud had forged a lie against him, and involved him in many Troubles, when in the mean time, their heart was as fat as grease. They wallowed in Ease and Pleasure, but David kept right with God; and yet his Afflictions do not cease. God doth not presently take away Opposition, because of our proud, unhumbled, unmortified Spirits, though we hold fast our Integrity for the main: therefore he comforteth himself in his spiritual Protection under the Affliction, though the Affliction was not removed. It is good, &c.

In the words there is
1. An Assertion, It is good for me that I have been afflicted.
2. The Reason, that I might learn thy Statutes. Or, Here is a general Truth explained by a particular Instance. In the general he saith it is good, and then what good he got by it.
